explanation: Memoize edit distances between prefixes. Empty prefixes need the other prefix’s length in insertions or deletions. Equal trailing characters share the shorter-prefix distance; unequal characters try substitution, insertion and deletion.
timeComplexity: O(mn) worst case for nonempty strings: at most mn prefix pairs and constant transitions per pair. Empty-prefix bases take O(1) logical work. There are at most (m+1)(n+1) prefix pairs with three predecessor choices; iterative code keeps two short rows.
spaceComplexity: O(mn+m+n): memo storage plus up to O(m+n) recursive frames; fixed table implementations allocate the full mn table. Iterative variants keep two rows over the shorter string; memoized variants retain prefix-pair states and recursive frames.

correctness: Any optimal edit sequence for unequal final characters ends in one of those three operations; each reduces to the corresponding smaller-prefix problem and costs one. Conversely each candidate builds a valid sequence. Taking their minimum is therefore exact, and matching trailing characters need no edit.
walkthrough: To turn "cat" into "cut", keep c, substitute a with u, and keep t. The prefix recurrence charges exactly one substitution, so the result is 1. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: An empty string requires inserting or deleting every character of the other string.
Substitution costs one, rather than a deletion plus insertion.
